memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When morning came, there was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, 'What is this you have done to me? I served you for Rachel, didn't I? Why have you deceived me?' Laban replied, 'It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one. Finish this daughter's bridal week; then we will give you the younger one also, in return for another seven years of work.'" - Gen 29:25-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When morning light reveals the truth, Jacob is outraged: "Why have you deceived me?" His protest is completely understandable — he had been wronged. But listen closely to Laban's explanation: "It is not our custom to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older one." Those words must have pierced Jacob's heart, for he was the younger who had grasped what belonged to the older. Laban unknowingly held up a mirror to Jacob's own past.

There is a humbling lesson here. Jacob, so indignant at being deceived, had done the very same to others. It is easy to be furious at wrongs done to us while forgetting the wrongs we have done. We feel the sting of others' deception far more sharply than we ever felt our own.

When we are wronged, God sometimes uses the moment to gently show us ourselves. Jacob's cry, "Why have you deceived me?" is the very question his own father might have asked him. Perhaps, in that painful morning, Jacob began to understand the pain he had caused.

Before we nurse our outrage at how others treat us, it is worth pausing to ask: have I done the same? God's discipline often works this way — holding up a mirror, so that we might see ourselves honestly and change.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I feel others' wrongs more sharply than my own?
2. Is God using a hurt in my life to show me something about myself?
3. Where do I need to see myself honestly in the mirror?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I am wronged, keep me from self-righteous outrage. Help me to see myself honestly, to own my own faults, and to grow into a person of integrity. Amen.
